Estimates are based on what I know of NAS-Bench-201's structure. I did not query the benchmark data.

- **Replace-type conditions (k = j).** Pairs 10, 12 and 15 have the strongest priors. Swapping a weak op such as avg_pool or none for skip or a conv helps more than swapping out a conv. Removing a skip on edge 3 hurts more than most other replacements.
- **Weak parent cells.** When the parent already has pooling or none on the main paths (pairs 2, 7, 17, 20, 23, 24, 28), adding a conv gains more. Removing or pooling another path hurts more.
- **Dependence through node 1.** Edges 2 and 4 only matter as much as edge 0 makes node 1 informative. This drives the mild leanings in pairs 0, 9 and 18.
- **Everything else** has no strong mechanism, so N dominates.
